subject: ela
intro: Phonological awareness is the ability to hear and work with the sounds in spoken words. You do not need to look at letters — you only listen! Key skills include: telling whether words rhyme, counting syllables (chunks) in a word, hearing the first sound in a word, blending separate sounds into a word, and segmenting a word into its individual sounds. This lesson covers all of these skills.

items.prompt: Do 'cat' and 'hat' rhyme? How do you know?

steps: Two words rhyme when they end with the same sound.
Because the endings sound the same, the words rhyme.
solution.answer: Yes, 'cat' and 'hat' rhyme. They both end with the /at/ sound.

items.prompt: How many syllables (chunks) are in the word 'butterfly'? Clap as you say it.

steps: Say the word slowly and clap each chunk: BUT - ter - fly.
Clap 1 for 'BUT', clap 2 for 'ter', clap 3 for 'fly'.
You clapped 3 times, so there are 3 syllables.

items.prompt: What is the FIRST sound in the word 'ship'?

steps: Say 'ship' slowly and listen to the very first sound.
The first sound in 'ship' is /sh/ — the 'sh' digraph makes one sound.

items.prompt: Blend these sounds together to make a word: /f/ - /r/ - /o/ - /g/. What word is it?

steps: Say each sound one after another, running them together.
When you blend /f/-/r/-/o/-/g/ you get the word 'frog'.

items.prompt: Segment the word 'plan' into its individual sounds. How many sounds does it have?

Which word rhymes with 'sun'?
A) sit
B) fun
C) ran
items.hint: Listen to the ending sound of 'sun' — it ends with /un/. Which answer also ends with /un/?

items.prompt:
How many syllables are in 'rabbit'? Clap it out.
A) 1
B) 2
C) 3
items.hint: Say 'rabbit' slowly and clap each part: rab - bit.

steps: Say 'rabbit' and clap each chunk: rab (1) - bit (2).

items.prompt:
What is the LAST sound in the word 'map'?
A) /m/
B) /a/
C) /p/
items.hint: Say 'map' slowly and listen to the very end of the word.

steps: The last sound you hear is /p/.
solution.answer: C) The last sound in 'map' is /p/.

items.prompt: Blend these sounds: /s/ - /t/ - /o/ - /p/. What word do you get?

How many sounds are in the word 'chip'?
A) 2
B) 3
C) 4
items.hint: Remember: 'ch' makes ONE sound, /ch/. Segment each sound separately.

steps: 'ch' is one sound, 'i' is one sound, 'p' is one sound.
